Phase 5 · the opening · 13 October 2026

The gridlock opening

The game starts with nothing local running and the roads jammed. The first thing you do is reopen Stockport, and from then on every station, train and bus stop takes cars off the road: the traffic easing on the map is the score. Static mockups, phones first: the map is drawn from the game’s own network data (its stand-in roads, the M60’s course, the river and the line), the figures from the design’s model. Nothing here is the game. The write-up: docs/design/gridlock.md. Buying, rethought · Back to the game.

For the owner Open questions

Each with the option the build takes if there’s no answer.

  1. Starting cash and the price of reopening. £4,000 to start, Reopen Stockport £1,000: after the first tap the game stands where today’s starts (a halt, £3,000), only sooner.
  2. Every station starts shut, and buying one is “Reopen”. Yes: the same buy with a new word on a station’s card. Stops and routes that never existed keep Buy.
  3. Does the jam push people onto the trains? Not in the first build: the car figure is worked out from journeys the sim already models and changes nothing it does. Slow roads sending more people to the trains is a later part, with its own balance run.
  4. A reward for cars taken off the road. No cash: fares already pay for every rider. If it should count for something, reputation is the cheapest place.
  5. A traffic figure in the top bar. No: cash and the clock only (320 px). The score is on the map, the Network card and each road’s card.
  6. The M60. It eases slowly and is the last road to clear: most of its traffic goes round Manchester. The main line takes it from coral to amber.
  7. Trains that aren’t the player’s. The expresses keep running through without stopping. What’s shut is the local network.
  8. How a later start is chosen. A Starts branch of perks on the renewal sheet; each start bought is offered beside Stockport when the next contract begins. The first game has no choice. A start is data (which places are open, the camera, the held trains), so Piccadilly, a bus start or the Marple line need no new code.

The model

  • Who drives: everyone who’d make a trip but whom the network doesn’t carry yet, 72% of them at the wheel (Stockport’s census). Before Stockport reopens that’s everyone.
  • Where: each road stretch (the A6 by Mersey Square, Heaton Chapel, Levenshulme, Longsight, Ardwick and south to Hazel Grove; the M60 by junction 1) carries the trips along it and traffic the network never touches, against a capacity from the Department for Transport’s 2024 counts (the M60 at junction 1, 147,744 vehicles a day; the A6 by Merseyway, 19,796).
  • Gridlock: past capacity a queue grows by the excess and drains when the load falls. The opening starts at 125% on the A6 and 120% on the M60.
  • Derived, never stepped: nothing the sim does reads it, so pacing holds; it loads after the first frame.
  • Faster to the first fare: today the first fare comes about 200 real seconds in; here about 15, as the train is already standing at platform 4.

On load: 0 s

Nothing local is running. Stockport is shut: a shutter across the Station Road entrance, the stopper dark at platform 4, a few people waiting on the forecourt. Wellington Road is nose to tail over Mersey Square with its brake lights lit, the M60 crawls both ways under the viaduct, and the roads are washed coral. One bright price on the map, Reopen · £1,000, and one card in the sheet. No tutorial: it’s the only bright thing there is.

Reopened: about 15 s

The player tapped Reopen. The shutter is up, the platform lamps and the board are on, the stopper’s windows are warm and its doors are open; the crowd walked in and boards, and the cash pill counts up with every fare. Heaton Chapel’s price turns bright with its meter now it touches what the player owns. The card is the halt’s card: four stages. At the back of the queue on Wellington Road a few cars have turned off and not come back.

One minute in

The first train crosses the viaduct, moving over the stopped M60: the shot that says what the game is. Its fares paid about £4,100; the player bought the subway (£2,000) the moment they looked at the card, and Platform 3 has appeared. On Wellington Road the queue has stopped growing so fast; nothing else changes on its own. The next train is about ten real minutes away, as today.

Three game days in

The main line is open to Piccadilly with its stages bought. At this height the cars are too small to draw, so the roads carry the wash alone: the A6 from Mersey Square to Ardwick has cooled to clear and pale amber, busy but moving. The A6 south through Davenport and Hazel Grove is still coral (the Hazel Grove line isn’t open), and the M60 has only gone from coral to amber: most of its traffic goes round Manchester, not along the line. The Network card leads with the score.

Tap the traffic: a road’s card

Day 2’s morning peak, Stockport and Heaton Chapel open. Tapping the queue on Wellington Road South opens the road’s card at half height: four figures, the drive now against free-flowing, and the places along it. A road is a place that’s never bought (until bus lanes, step 12), and its card recommends nothing: Next to lists what touches it, owned or fogged with its price, as every card does.

What’s drawn where

Near the camera, cars: up to 300, ten triangles each, instanced, no shadows, standing in queues back from each junction with their brake lights lit, moving at the road’s speed elsewhere. Everywhere else, a wash: the streets the ground already paints, tinted by how full each road is, from a 64 × 64 texture. Zero triangles.
